about: Which income-tax schedules, standard deductions and wage bases move with prices or pay each year, by jurisdiction (money-tax-brackets-and-benefits-not-indexed-to-prices). Read into each starting law row's terms as `indexed` by src/core2/laws-starting.ts; the paycheck rule (src/core2/tax-withholding.ts) scales the row's dollar amounts by it.

income-tax.source: 26 U.S.C. 1(f) (brackets adjusted each year for the cost of living) and 63(c)(4) (standard deduction); IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 states the 2026 amounts.

social-security-tax.source: 42 U.S.C. 430(b): the contribution and benefit base rises each year with the national average wage index.

medicare-tax.source: 26 U.S.C. 3101(b)(2): the additional Medicare tax threshold ($200,000 single) is not indexed.

states.source: Tax Foundation, 2026 State Individual Income Tax Rates and Brackets (taxfoundation.org/data/all/state/state-income-tax-rates-2026/), footnotes d, j, n and bb: 'Bracket levels adjusted for inflation each year' and 'Standard deduction and/or personal exemption is adjusted annually for inflation.' Footnote u (deductions tied to the federal amounts, which are indexed) adds AZ, ID, ME, MO, MT, NM, ND, SC and DC to the deductions.
